pages.text: "That red one! I'll pick it!" Leo the know-it-all fox jumped under an apple tree. Several apples still hung on a high branch. The low ones were already picked.
Rudi the hungry squirrel held the branch and pulled it down. "Leo, I'll pull. You pick!" The branch bent, bringing an apple right before their noses.
Leo lifted his muzzle. "I can do that alone. Move!" He shoved Rudi aside. Rudi landed on their bottom. The branch sprang back up.
"Don't push!" Rudi brushed off their orange apron and sat under the tree with their back turned. The other three watching went downhill too. Leo stood alone.
Leo jumped and jumped, but his fingertips couldn't reach. Pull the branch with one hand, and there was no hand left to pick. Leo gave the tree a little kick.
Grandma Bear came under the tree and spread a big hand. "Leo, how many hands do you need for that one apple?" Leo quietly looked down at his two hands.
Rudi was sitting under the tree. Leo stood in front of them. "Sorry I pushed you. I can't pick it alone. Will you help?" Rudi rose, swishing their big tail. "Don't push—use words!"
Rudi pulled the branch down, and Leo reached out. Two hands for one apple. Pop! Leo twisted off the reddest apple.
The three came back uphill. Leo called loudly, "One, hands down! Two, use words! Three, pick together!" All five took turns pulling and picking, until every remaining apple was picked.
Grandma sat under the tree with Leo and Rudi on either side. "Hands that push to take are empty. Hands called with words become two." Leo bit the apple. Crunch! "Don't push—use words!"
